scope: Proposals 0002/0003 and relevant selected Define/Lab runtime interfaces; not a production security assessment

findings.title: The proposed formal meaning needs an unambiguous interpretation
findings.observation: The Pack formula omits grouping around quantified clauses and the reference-resolution disjunction. ValidationScopeDeclared(V) can be read as part of only the DeclaredGap branch. ExactlyOne(delta(c) in D) has no specified typed interpretation. Existing language checks accept supplied distinction rationales and reject normalized textual collisions; they are not semantic equivalence or full-consistency proofs.
findings.risk: A structurally valid Definition could receive conflicting formal interpretations or a stronger non-collapse claim than its evidence supports.
recommended_amendment: Group every quantified clause; declare delta:C->D and matching payloads explicitly, with validation scope outside the disjunction.
Bind each required predicate/signature to an operational or selected formal interpretation.

Declare the assurance claim class and coverage: structural, finite interpreted model, owner fidelity review, or stronger supported proof. Do not rename a lexical/rationale check as formal non-collapse.
findings.must_resolve_before: semantic promotion readiness and exact Definition owner decision
future_verification: Counterexamples: all references resolved with validation scope absent; unresolved reference without a declared gap; two differently worded statements with the same meaning.
Check interpretation against all three voices and declared neighboring/current definitions; record unsupported source clauses.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Key possession is not yet bound to the semantic principal
findings.observation: A local store accepts an explicit owner_ref and public key; signature verification proves that configured key signed the local envelope. The work map requests role/principal/assignment evidence but does not specify who establishes the trusted key-to-principal binding. Durable actor access and user confirmation are caller declarations.
findings.risk: A matching owner label and valid local signature could be mistaken for an actual semantic-owner determination when new authorization code is added.
recommended_amendment: Select an explicit trust root: the existing exact human owner-decision route, or a separately admitted principal/key enrollment or delegation binding.
Keep operator key, semantic principal, owner role, assignment and decision source independently represented.
Treat actor_ref, allowed_effects and user_confirmed as declarations unless their authentication basis is established. Do not create an authentication service merely to fill these fields.
findings.must_resolve_before: semantic authorization or repository application; read-only candidate work can proceed
future_verification: A valid local key with a copied definition-owner label is rejected for semantic promotion.
Unbound, rotated or revoked keys cannot make new effects; historical approved effects retain their exact recorded basis.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Source parsing can use different bytes from the recorded digest

evidence.selector: Capture.read, lines 82-92; final freshness in capture, lines 294-301

findings.observation: Capture.read hashes f.read_bytes(), then JSON loading reopens the path. Final freshness checks current bytes, but the parsed document was not necessarily parsed from the hashed byte buffer. A transient A -> B -> A change can evade a later A-byte comparison.
findings.risk: The successor may bind a source digest to document content it did not actually hash. This is a static race possibility, not a reproduced exploit or claim about current admitted data.
recommended_amendment: Strictly decode/parse the exact byte buffer that was hashed; reject duplicate keys and nonfinite values from that buffer.
Read immutable selected epoch material or pin one snapshot/descriptor for the capture.
Carry parsed-content and file-byte identity consistently through source/reference validation.
findings.must_resolve_before: using successor source capture as authorization evidence
future_verification: Planned controlled writer-interleaving case checks that parsed content always corresponds to the captured digest.
Persistent and transient source changes must cause a clean retry/failure or remain outside the pinned immutable snapshot.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Repository publication has no chosen coherent commit boundary
findings.observation: The local runtime stages a transaction then atomically advances one HEAD. The plan extends this to repository registry, index, drift, profiles, current lookup and Project State, but does not choose how readers observe those multiple files as one committed epoch. A store lock does not lock arbitrary repository edits.
findings.risk: Readers may see mixed epochs or fail during cutover; crash recovery could leave authorized records and current lookup inconsistent. Rechecking sources immediately before commit does not prevent a later external write.
recommended_amendment: Choose a concrete repository publication protocol: immutable epoch directory plus one accepted selection pointer, or another explicit staged/CAS protocol with a recoverable single visibility boundary.
Specify lock/CAS coverage, immutable preimages, reader snapshot selection and external-edit detection.
Keep schema/code/profile selection compatible throughout publication; do not describe independent per-file replacement as whole-repository atomicity.
future_verification: Planned reader-during-cutover, competing writer, stale preimage and crash-at-each-publication-step cases.
After recovery, readers see a complete old or complete new selected epoch, or an explicit unavailable state; no mixed state is labeled current.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: The future source epoch depends on records not yet created

evidence.selector: consequences: authorization_sha256, governance records and history

findings.observation: G09.02 prepares an exact successor reader/profile before the later decision. That epoch includes post-approval authorization, history and state material. Actual signature/timestamp-dependent bytes do not exist during early preparation. The task graph is acyclic, but these content dependencies are not specified.
findings.risk: A prospective profile may contain unresolved hashes, use fixture hashes as real outcomes, or require its own future authorization digest. No actual digest cycle is asserted; the design must rule one out.
recommended_amendment: Separate the manifest of immutable reviewed inputs from declared generated consequences and observed application receipts.
Authorize exact inputs, selected effects, deterministic generator/version and preconditions; identify legitimately post-decision fields explicitly.
Describe when final source-profile/selection bytes are materialized and how their authority derives, without a self-referential digest or second implicit approval.
findings.must_resolve_before: freezing the adoption manifest and authorizing epoch advancement
future_verification: Fixture-dependent, predicted and observed digests cannot be substituted for each other.
A content-dependency graph distinguishes reviewed inputs, decision evidence and generated outputs; no output must hash itself.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Cross-runtime parsing and hash rules remain unspecified
findings.observation: Node uses JSON.stringify of sorted-key objects; Python uses json.dumps with its own number formatting and strict persisted-file loading. The CLI reads JSON with JSON.parse, which does not retain duplicate key occurrences. Current authority signatures are Python-owned; the proposed cross-runtime evidence/core protocol has no explicit serialization ownership.
findings.risk: The same conceptual record can have different semantic digests, and duplicate-key input can be interpreted differently from the text a reviewer saw. This is a protocol risk, not a reproduced failure of current string-only context epochs.
recommended_amendment: Choose one normative serialization/digest owner, or a fully specified shared serialization with numeric/string restrictions.
Distinguish raw-file hashes from normalized record digests and signature bytes.
Require strict duplicate-key rejection at external boundaries before JSON.parse discards duplicates; define allowed number precision and normalization explicitly.
future_verification: Planned cross-runtime cases: 1 versus 1.0, exponent forms, negative zero, unsafe integers, Unicode and numeric-looking keys.
Duplicate keys and unsupported nonfinite/precision values fail before review; source text and normalized content remain traceable.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Verification can precede a required binding and late documentation

evidence.selector: G10.01/G10.02 do not depend on G02.05; G10.04 follows G10.02

findings.observation: The exact CLI realization binding G02.05 is not a dependency or ancestor of the verification matrix or frozen prototype verification. Documentation is prepared after prototype verification, and there is no explicit check of the final documentation/adoption closure.
findings.risk: Tests can be recorded for a candidate that lacks its claimed realization binding; late docs may describe unverified commands or mismatched scope.
recommended_amendment: Add G02.05 as a dependency of G10.01.
Add a final documentation/adoption-closure check after G10.04 and before G10.05.
Bind every verification result to its input manifest; a later code, contract or behavior change reopens the relevant verification and invalidates affected decisions.
findings.must_resolve_before: Product review and final adoption decisions
future_verification: Prototype verification cannot be ready while the realization binding is pending.
Exact documented CLI commands, relative links and stated behavior are checked on final selected bytes.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: A completed decision task does not mean its outcome permits continuation

evidence.selector: G10.03 completion includes approve/revise/defer/reject; G10.05 depends on task completion

findings.observation: The DAG describes prerequisites and pending statuses, but no transition predicates. G10.03 finishes when any owner outcome is recorded, including rejection. The work map calls for rebuilding closure after partial selections but does not define explicit revise/defer/reject branches or approval invalidation after changed bytes.
findings.risk: An executor could treat recorded rejection as a satisfied prerequisite, or reuse old evidence after a revision. There is no such executor behavior claimed today.
recommended_amendment: Add explicit guards for qualifying Product approval and each independent owner effect.
Define revise -> new candidate epoch -> impacted verification -> new decision; defer/reject stop only the dependent branch.
Compute accepted-subset dependency closure and require an exact newly reviewable bundle when target membership or bytes change.
future_verification: Rejected/deferred Product or semantic outcomes never reach their dependent apply effect.
Partial selection preserves unselected targets; changed-byte requests cannot reuse an old decision/core/bundle.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Legacy compile and durable-session consumers need explicit adapters
findings.observation: The active pack validator accepts only the legacy pack discriminator. Alch handoff requires no open questions and lowers every disposition. Session/store discriminators remain v1. The map proposes versioning and partial/use-specific readiness, but does not enumerate these consumers as a concrete compatibility matrix.
findings.risk: A new pack may validate for preparation yet be rejected or misinterpreted by compile/resume. Relaxing a global ready flag could accidentally allow unsupported compile input.
recommended_amendment: Choose an explicit supported route for every consumer: legacy preservation, versioned adapter, or visible unsupported result.
Retain compile-specific readiness unless an exact selected subset and compiler contract support it.
Specify identity/revision/lineage across conversions and saved session resume; do not coerce a new schema label to an old one.
future_verification: Planned old/new pack x prepare/compile/resume compatibility cases.
Open questions may be reviewable while unsupported compilation remains blocked; numeric/boolean Calculation regressions still run on the selected compiler.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Semantic revision impact is not closed over declared consumers

evidence.selector: post-staging validation of active relations/carrier Definition references, lines 200-217

findings.observation: The map compares selected semantic neighbors and requests affected consumers, but does not construct the dependency inventory for a foundational Definition revision or other changed meanings. Existing runtime validation focuses on target records, active typed relations and carrier Definition references; narrative and application consumers are not all covered.
findings.risk: A meaning can be revised while current profiles, carriers, policies, other Definitions or docs retain an incompatible exact meaning. Two terms can remain semantically redundant despite different wording.
recommended_amendment: Build an exact declared consumer/dependency impact manifest across current Definitions, carriers, profiles, policies, mappings, sessions and documentation.
For every affected reference select preserve-historical, proven-compatible, update, deprecate, block or explicitly deferred residue with owner.
Declare the scope of consistency/non-collapse assurance; current-source coverage and known interpretation gaps must remain visible rather than promising whole-repository proof.
findings.must_resolve_before: a foundational Definition successor or any semantic revision admission
future_verification: An incompatible declared dependent blocks current promotion/adoption until repaired or explicitly governed.
A preserved historical binding stays exact; it is not silently rewritten to the new current version.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: Pack and assurance work has no declared resource bounds

evidence.selector: new closed pack and supplemental contracts

findings.observation: Chat limits some arrays and context has an inline budget, but the new scripted pack/supplement/reference graph and semantic impact work have no selected limits. Pair checking grows with the number of terms; recursive references and saved session history add separate costs.
findings.risk: Large input may consume excessive memory or time, or be truncated in a way that hides incomplete semantic coverage.
recommended_amendment: Declare file/output bytes, concept count, reference depth, pair-check budget, history size and timeout limits for the intended release.
Use explicit batches and residue/continuation records when the full declared set exceeds a bound.
Never report full required-concept coverage after silent truncation.
findings.must_resolve_before: declaring production-like bounded operation or scaling beyond current fixtures
future_verification: Boundary and over-limit inputs produce clear bounded outcomes.
Batch recomposition preserves full declared required-set identity and unresolved residue.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

findings.title: The first useful preview is tied to the entire authority implementation

evidence.selector: G05.06 freeze depends on governance, transaction and context completion

findings.observation: The full candidate freeze waits for independent governance records, transaction compatibility and refreshed views. The map lacks a separate bounded frozen preview milestone, although complete non-mutating candidate preparation could be reviewed earlier.
findings.risk: Sixty-seven items can become a single large change before users inspect real output, increasing feedback cost and the risk of unnecessary generic runtime work.
recommended_amendment: Declare three delivery milestones: read-only preparation preview; guarded exact review; authorized application with epoch/view refresh.
Freeze each candidate surface separately with exact limitations; keep the single final admission scope reviewable if that remains the selected interaction model.
Constrain the first writer/adapter to this Definition integration and defer general admission-platform work unless a concrete target requires it.
findings.must_resolve_before: starting broad implementation scheduling; does not block draft review
future_verification: The preview can be demonstrated without signing, stores, repository mutation or new authority.
Every milestone has a bounded accepted/deferred scope; partial delivery is never reported as full integration.
findings.confidence: static repository/plan evidence; failure scenarios not executed

overall_disposition: Planning structure is coherent, but semantic admission and authorized application are not ready. Resolve phase-specific critical/high findings and amend the plan before implementation reaches those boundaries.
